title: From Crop to Beam: Post-Processing a High-Contrast Landscape Shot

date.basis: Embedded creation time in metadata; folder/file naming indicates 2026 session; transcript corroborates mid-2020s workflow.

summary: This video is a hands-on teardown of post-processing a high-contrast landscape image. The author details a sequence of decisions beginning with tight cropping and perspective warp, then expands tonal range while preserving detail through a two-pass color grade. The workflow emphasizes directional light development, horizon-driven color balance, and layer separation via selective blues. The tutor also demonstrates fine-tuning with dodge/burn, glow, and edge treatments, and culminates with advanced elements such as beam creation and careful compositing (including a bird insertion) plus pre-processing steps like noise reduction. The narrative stresses starting from a darker baseline, maintaining a forward path toward light rather than repeatedly brightening disparate regions, and using large-brush tools for cohesive, natural results.

sections.title: Cropping, edge alignment and perspective correction
sections.description: The shot is cropped to the edges of the foreground trees, then perspective warp is used to align elements and establish a trapezoidal correction so bushes appear to lean inward.

sections.title: Dynamic range planning and initial light development
sections.description: Dynamic range is expanded, then the exposure is adjusted downward to create a controlled, single-direction light flow. The original image is blended back in to refine tonal balance while keeping a directional light path.

sections.title: Color grading, horizon emphasis and blues handling
sections.description: Color grading is performed more than once to achieve the desired range. A white adjustment and subtle warmth lay the foundation, followed by a second pass to refine the overall color balance, with blues extracted to separate foreground layers from the distant hills behind trees.

sections.title: Glow, light bleed, and foreground texture enhancement
sections.description: Subtle glow is introduced to hint at light slipping through the scene and a light bleed is shaped to guide the viewer through the horizon while large brushes texture and balance the foreground.

sections.title: Refinement: dodges, halos, and minor crops
sections.description: Mid-tone and highlight dodges draw attention to key areas (notably water) while halos are removed and the composition is gently cropped for symmetry and visual flow.

sections.title: Bird insertion and pre-processing notes
sections.description: The editor discusses identifying a bird, placing it via Healing Stamp, cleaning dust, and noting the need for noise reduction due to ISO levels prior to processing.

sections.title: Beam creation technique and final touches
sections.description: A focused walkthrough of constructing and color-matching beams, painting them into the scene, and erasing the opposite side to emphasize the beam without overdoing it. The tutor emphasizes color accuracy and selective placement as a key control on form.
